The basics for dual boot: install Windows first, install linux using a partition of the drive, then install Grub Customiser (or another MBR modifier).

Hi. I've got an old pc I want to repurpose. Wondering if it is possible/feasible to achieve both of the following with one PC:

-A htpc running kodi, and that can also run network media files. E.g., wife downloads crap tv show on her laptop, and plays it in kodi on the htpc (instead of hooking laptop up to tv via hdm cable)

-A personal cloud storage for files, including a git repository so I can work on code / writing remotely via ssh from my many devices.

I guess my main Q is: does doing one of the above compromise my ability to do the other?

Thx <3

Probably not. As long as the old PC is equipped with enough CPU, RAM and storage space to run all the services you want, and it has enough sockets (USB etc.) to connect any and all peripheral devices you require, you should be fine.

You can indeed do both with the same machine.

What you'd want to do ideally is to have a solid-state drive as your root (system) drive, and a RAID array of platter drives to use as a Network Attached Storage device. In this way, you can access the RAID array from the network directly, and you can (through Kodi) share the media via UPnP.

Cool. Thanks for the 'ideally'. I've built a couple of Pcs but have no experience with RAID. Will this approach depend on the motherboard of my pc? I can't check the model right now, it's a mini ITX rig with an AMD a4 APU and a MSI mobo. I've got one SSD in there but can probably fit more storage with some fiddling. It's a pretty small case so I'm restricted in terms of case space to add storage.

What are the downsides of not using RAID for this if the rig doesn't support it?

RAID provides speed and/or redundancy. You'd lose out on either multiple people enjoying data from the same volume and/or fault tolerance.

What is the motherboard model? The mini-itx APU-based MSI mobos I'm familiar with don't support RAID controllers as a planar device, and only have one pci-e slot, which you probably don't want to fill with a RAID controller. RAID controllers would provide a great performance benefit over a software-controlled RAID setup.

In that case, I'd probably set up a discrete backend server as a NAS device with some tuner cards for recording off the line/air. If that's too much, two SSDs in RAID 1 (mirroring) mode would probably see some speed improvement over a single drive (even with software RAID control), and you'd have two physical copies of the data for fault-tolerance. This would require 3 SSDs (one for system drive, two of the exact same kind for cloud storage). This would be expensive, however as high-capacity SSDs are still not cheap.

IF the motherboard doesn't support hardware raid, you can configure software raid across multiple disk devices with mdadm. I know its software raid, that isn't ran on a specifically coded asic, and is taking CPU cycles to achieve the raid. From my experience with it, its lightweight enough to where there shouldn't be a problem with using it.

I have seen it used in enterprises to run openstack servers, so it should be sufficient for a home server. It is what i run across my 6* 3 TB spinning rust while i run the OS on an SSD.
